goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection risk in migration due to string interpolation of host values in the `execute` INSERT statement

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, host values are read from the `site_settings` table (`val = embeddable_hosts[0]['value']`, split into `records`), then inserted via raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. `h` is not quoted/escaped, so if the stored setting contains a single quote or crafted SQL (e.g., `evil.com'); DROP TABLE embeddable_hosts; --`), the generated SQL becomes syntactically altered and could execute unintended statements. This is a verifiable injection/SQL-breaking risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` in migration drops existing table data if re-run

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which instructs Rails to drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. While the table won’t exist on a normal first-time deploy, this option makes the migration unnecessarily destructive and would cause data loss if the migration is ever run against a DB where `embeddable_hosts` already exists (e.g., manual table creation, a previous/partial migration, or re-running after tampering with `schema_migrations`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddableHost#host` lacks uniqueness validation and a unique database index, allowing duplicate hosts

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost` only has `validates_format_of :host` and no `validates :host, uniqueness: ...`. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `t.string :host, null: false` but does not add a unique index on `host` (or on `lower(host)`). The admin controller `save_host` writes `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and saves without any duplicate check, so duplicate rows for the same host are allowed by both app-level validation and DB constraints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs only test inheritance and lack tests for CRUD, authorization, or error handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs: `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`. Each contains only a single example asserting the controller is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`, and does not exercise any endpoints (`create/update/destroy/show/update`), staff-only access, parameter validation, or failure/error behavior. No other specs in the diff cover these controllers’ CRUD/authorization/error paths, so the finding is directly verifiable from the added tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddingController#update` is a no-op and represents dead code

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` indeed does not mutate anything; it just re-serializes `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`) and ignores any incoming params. However, calling it “dead code” isn’t strictly verifiable from the diff: a PUT route is added and the Ember controller has a `saveChanges()` action that would call `embedding.update({})`, but the provided `embedding.hbs` template doesn’t invoke `saveChanges` (no save button/form), so there’s no clear demonstrated broken behavior—just an endpoint that currently acts as a no-op placeholder. That’s more of an incomplete/unused feature than a definite defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddableHost#record_for_host` returns mixed types (`false` and `nil`) for different error cases

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns `false` for invalid/missing URI/host (`return false unless ...`) and returns an AR object or `nil` when the lookup finds nothing (`where(...).first`). That is a mixed return type, but it does not create a verifiable defect in this diff: all current callers shown treat both `false` and `nil` equivalently (e.g., `host_allowed?` uses `.present?`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` which yields `nil` for both `false` and `nil`). So the finding is more of an API-consistency nit than a real introduced bug/correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `_focusOnInput` runs on initial insert even when not editing, attempting to focus a non-existent element

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `_focusOnInput` is decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`, so it will run once on insert even if `editing` is false. However, when not editing, the template does not render an element with class `.host-name`, and `this.$('.host-name')` will return an empty jQuery collection. Calling `.focus()` on an empty jQuery set is a no-op (does not throw), so this does not constitute a real, verifiable bug—at most it is a harmless/unnecessary call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message in `embed_controller.rb` is misleading, always saying "invalid referer host" even when no hosts are configured

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the previous logic explicitly raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set')` when no hosts were configured (`SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?`). The diff removes that check and now always raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('invalid referer host')` unless `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. When there are zero `EmbeddableHost` records configured, `host_allowed?` will return false for any referer (or nil), causing the same "invalid referer host" message even though the real issue is that no embeddable hosts are configured. This is a verifiable behavior change introduced by the diff.
